blueprints.subject: maths
blueprints.title: Place value to 10,000
blueprints.objective: Reads, writes, compares and decomposes whole numbers up to 10,000.
blueprints.teach: Read multi-digit numbers from the greatest place value. Decompose them into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones before comparing.
blueprints.workedExample: In 5,482, what value does the digit 5 represent? The 5 is in the thousands place, so its value is 5,000.

guidedTry.prompt: In 5,482, what value does the digit 5 represent?
guidedTry.hintLevel1: Name the place of the digit 5.
guidedTry.hintLevel2: The 5 is in the thousands place, so its value is 5,000.

masteryTransfer.prompt: A stadium count is 9,408 and another is 9,480. Which count is larger?

blueprints.reviewPrompt: Later, try a fresh place value to 10,000 task and explain the clue, rule or evidence you used.
blueprints.narrationText: Read multi-digit numbers from the greatest place value. Decompose them into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones before comparing.

blueprints.subject: maths
blueprints.title: Measurement and perimeter
blueprints.objective: Measures, converts within familiar units and reasons about perimeter in simple contexts.
blueprints.teach: Perimeter is the distance around a shape. Use consistent units and add every side length once.
blueprints.workedExample: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter in centimetres? Perimeter = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm.

guidedTry.prompt: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter in centimetres?
guidedTry.hintLevel1: Add all four side lengths.
guidedTry.hintLevel2: Perimeter = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm.

masteryTransfer.prompt: A triangular garden has sides 4 m, 5 m and 6 m. What is its perimeter?

blueprints.reviewPrompt: Later, try a fresh measurement and perimeter task and explain the clue, rule or evidence you used.
blueprints.narrationText: Perimeter is the distance around a shape. Use consistent units and add every side length once.

blueprints.subject: maths
blueprints.title: Time and money problems

blueprints.teach: For elapsed time, move forward in hours and minutes. For money, add costs or subtract from the amount paid and keep rupees consistent.

guidedTry.prompt: How many minutes pass from 2:15 to 3:00?
guidedTry.hintLevel1: Count forward to the next hour.
guidedTry.hintLevel2: From 2:15 to 3:00 is 45 minutes.

blueprints.narrationText: For elapsed time, move forward in hours and minutes. For money, add costs or subtract from the amount paid and keep rupees consistent.

blueprints.subject: english
blueprints.title: Main ideas and simple inference
blueprints.objective: Identifies main ideas and makes a simple inference supported by details in a text.
blueprints.teach: Use the whole text for the main idea and point to a detail when making an inference. An inference must fit the evidence, not just a guess.
blueprints.workedExample: Leela carried a raincoat. Dark clouds covered the sky, and the wind grew cool. What can you infer? The raincoat, dark clouds and cool wind are details that support the inference that rain may be coming.

blueprints.reviewPrompt: Later, try a fresh main ideas and simple inference task and explain the clue, rule or evidence you used.
blueprints.narrationText: Use the whole text for the main idea and point to a detail when making an inference. An inference must fit the evidence, not just a guess.
